purpose: How an operator who refers or services small-business payroll clients runs the onboarding project that stands between a signed client and a correct first payroll: scoping the work against the client complexity class, establishing the entity and tax-account and authorization classes, migrating the employee roster, year-to-date balances, deductions and garnishment orders out of the prior system, setting up direct deposit and company funding, proving the configuration by parallel run and by reconciliation to already-filed returns before cutover, supervising the first live run, and handing off a compliance calendar and an evidence file with a named owner for every obligation across the platform, the service layer and the client.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the operator is a referral partner or a service layer working on top of a third-party payroll platform; the platform is the system of record and, where the client engages it as such, the tax filing and payment agent, while the operator is never the employer, never the tax preparer of record and never counsel

payroll obligations differ by federal, state and local jurisdiction and change over time, so every registration, deposit-frequency, filing, new-hire reporting, wage-notice and record-retention point in this knowledge base is an obligation CLASS whose current specifics must be verified in the client operating jurisdiction and against the platform current documentation before it is acted on

no figure is asserted here: platform fees, revenue-share terms, penalty exposure, deposit amounts and balance totals are described as the mechanism that produces a number and are verified per client against that client own records and the current partner-program terms

the client stays the employer of record and owns every determination reserved to an employer, including who is an employee, who is exempt, what each worker is paid, which benefits exist and whether a correction is filed

the data that moves during onboarding is the most sensitive a small employer holds, including legal names, social security numbers, dates of birth, home addresses, wage histories and bank credentials, and is handled least-privilege, time-boxed and on channels the client can audit
onboarding is a bounded project with a defined end: it stops at a signed handoff, after which the ongoing rhythm belongs to the recurring-relationship practice
exclusions: choosing between the referral-partner, reseller and service-bureau-on-platform business models and the obligations each carries, which belongs to the payroll referral models and client acquisition knowledge base

sourcing and selling clients: who refers payroll well, working bookkeeper, accountant, insurance and association referral relationships, the switching-pain sales conversation, and helping a prospect choose honestly between platforms before signing, all of which belong to the acquisition knowledge base

the recurring rhythm after go-live: the per-run pre-approval routine as an operating cadence, quarterly and annual filing cycles as calendar mechanisms in production, issue triage between client and platform, retention through error-free runs, and expansion into bookkeeping, HR or benefits referrals, all of which belong to the recurring relationship, compliance calendar and expansion knowledge base

tax, legal, accounting or employment-law advice of any kind; this is operator education about running a migration project, and every determination that belongs to the client or to a licensed adviser is routed to them

performing tax deposits, filings, amendments or agency representation; where the platform is engaged as filing and payment agent it performs them, and where it is not, the client and the client tax professional do
determinations reserved to the employer, including worker classification, exempt or non-exempt status, pay rates, benefit eligibility, leave entitlement and whether a discovered error is corrected

jurisdiction-specific specifics of any kind, including registration thresholds, account-number formats, local tax lists, deposit schedules, wage-notice wording and retention periods, which appear only as obligation classes to verify in the operating jurisdiction

invented numbers of any kind: platform pricing, per-employee fees, revenue-share percentages, penalty and interest amounts, market sizes and account values are described only as mechanisms and qualitative bands

the internal engineering of the payroll platform, including its calculation engine, filing systems and banking rails, which is treated as a documented black box whose boundary the operator maps rather than reverse-engineers
benefits brokerage, retirement plan administration, immigration or work-authorization opinions and HR advisory work, which are adjacent professions with their own licensing and are referred out

competency_questions.question: What is handed over when onboarding ends, to the client and to the ongoing service, and what evidence shows the project was done correctly?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLIANCE_CALENDAR_HANDOFF produces the obligation calendar with a named owner per item, PRIOR_PROVIDER_EXIT closes out the old system without a gap or a duplicate filing, and ONBOARDING_FILE_AND_SIGNOFF holds the authorizations, configuration record, reconciliation evidence and client sign-off

glossary.definition: The moment the new payroll system becomes the system of record for pay and for tax deposits, and the prior system stops producing them; the cutover date is chosen deliberately because it determines how much history has to be migrated and who is responsible for filings covering the period before it.

Recomputing a pay period that has already been paid by the prior system inside the new configuration and comparing the result line by line; it is a test of configuration rather than a payment, and its purpose is to surface a mis-set rate, deduction or tax setting while the run is still reversible on paper.

The accumulated per-employee and per-employer totals for the calendar year so far, including gross wages by category, each withheld tax, each employer tax, and every deduction and benefit accumulator; wage-base-limited taxes and annual-limit deductions compute wrongly for the rest of the year if these are loaded wrong.

Working an individual paycheck from gross pay through each tax and deduction to the net amount and proving that the two systems reach the same figure by the same path; a match on net alone can hide two errors that cancel, so the reconciliation is done line by line.

The cadence on which an employer must remit withheld payroll taxes to a given agency, assigned by that agency according to its own rules and subject to change; onboarding treats it as an attribute that must be read from the agency notice and configured in the platform rather than assumed or copied from another client.

The class of authorization by which an employer permits a payroll provider to access an agency account, file returns or move deposits on its behalf; the forms, scope and processing time differ by agency and jurisdiction and must be verified currently, and granting one never transfers the employer own liability.

Confirming that an employee or company bank account can actually receive or fund a transfer before payday depends on it, by whatever method the platform and bank support, such as a test transaction or a credential-based verification; unverified accounts are the ordinary cause of a first payday that does not land.

A payroll run outside the normal schedule, used to pay something that was missed or to correct a run that has already gone out; it carries its own tax and funding consequences and is the ordinary repair tool during the first weeks after cutover.

The dated list of recurring payroll obligation classes for a specific client, including per-run deposits, periodic returns, annual employee statements, new-hire reporting and rate-notice updates, each with the party responsible for it; onboarding builds it, and the recurring service practice operates it.

A court, agency or support order directing an employer to withhold from an employee wages and remit to a named recipient under rules the order itself carries; it is a legal instrument that continues across a change of payroll provider and does not pause because a migration is in progress.

nodes.definition: Onboarding is a dated project whose deadline the calendar sets rather than the client: the first live pay date, which cannot slip quietly because employees expect money on it. Framing the engagement means writing down what will exist at the end (a configured company, a migrated and validated roster, reconciled year-to-date balances, tested funding, a clean parallel run and a compliance calendar with an owner on every line), which of the three parties owes each input, and the date each input must arrive for the target go-live to survive. The frame carries a dependency register because onboarding almost never stalls on the operator work; it stalls on client-owed items such as an agency account number that has not been applied for, a prior-provider register nobody exported, a bank authorization waiting on a signature, or a benefit deduction schedule that lives in someone head. It also carries the stop rule that separates a professional practice from an accident: when a dependency slips past its date, the go-live date moves to the next clean boundary rather than the verification steps being compressed to protect it.

included: deliverable list for the onboarding project
dependency register with an owner and a due date per item
go-live date derivation and the stop rule that moves it
definition of project completion and handoff
excluded: the sales conversation that won the client
the ongoing service rhythm after handoff
pricing the engagement or the revenue-share arrangement

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: repeated onboardings that miss their first pay date for the same class of register item, which reprices the lead time that item is given

pros.claim: A dated dependency register makes a client-side delay visible while there is still time to move the date instead of compressing verification
pros.example: the state unemployment account number still not applied for in week two moves the go-live to the next period while employees can still be told

pros.claim: A written end state lets the project actually close instead of dissolving into months of unpaid configuration
pros.example: the operator closes onboarding at the signed calendar handoff rather than absorbing every later configuration request as still onboarding

cons.claim: A date fixed early creates a commitment that keeps being defended after the facts underneath it change
cons.example: discovering an employee working from a second state in week three while the original date is already announced to staff

cons.claim: Full project framing costs unbillable planning time that is hard to justify on the smallest clients
cons.example: a two-employee client where building the register takes about as long as the configuration itself

failure_modes: promising a go-live date before the complexity class is known
leaving items in the register with no named owner so nobody chases them
compressing the parallel run and reconciliation to protect an announced date
treating the platform advertised setup speed as the project plan for a client with real complexity
acceptance_tests: the register names every required input, its owner among platform, service layer and client, and the date it is needed by
the go-live date is derived from the complexity class and the longest agency or bank lead time in the register, and the stop rule is stated in writing
revisit_triggers: a register item passes its due date
a fact emerges that changes the complexity class, such as a worker in another state or an active withholding order
the client changes the desired first pay date

nodes.definition: Every duty in a payroll relationship belongs to exactly one of three parties, and the single most expensive onboarding defect is a duty that everyone assumed someone else held. The map is written explicitly: the platform calculates, moves money and, where engaged, files and deposits as agent; the service layer configures, migrates, verifies, reviews before approval and escalates; the client, as employer of record, supplies and approves the data, funds the account, makes every employer determination and remains liable for what is filed under its identification. The map is written duty by duty rather than as a slogan, covering who applies for agency accounts, who submits the pay data, who approves the run, who answers an employee pay question, who receives an agency notice and acts on it, who watches for a rate change, and who calls the platform when something breaks. It must also state the negatives, which are the lines the operator does not cross regardless of how convenient it would be: not signing returns as an officer of the client, not becoming the sole holder of the client agency credentials, not answering a question that requires a licensed adviser. The map is the parent of the compliance calendar, which is simply the same map with dates attached.

included: duty-by-duty assignment across platform, service layer and client
the explicit negatives the operator will not do
escalation path when a duty is contested
the source of ownership labels used by the compliance calendar
excluded: choosing the commercial model that sets which duties are available to the operator
platform internal responsibilities toward its own systems
the ongoing triage routine used after go-live

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a published change to the platform service description or partner agreement that moves a duty across the boundary

pros.claim: A duty-by-duty map removes the gap where an obligation silently has no owner
pros.example: the map forces an answer to who opens the mail from the state and acts on a rate notice, which is the classic ownerless duty

pros.claim: Written negatives protect the operator from drifting into work that belongs to a licensed profession or to the employer
pros.example: a client asking the operator to decide whether a long-time contractor should be on payroll is answered from the map rather than improvised

cons.claim: Clients often want the boundary blurred and read a firm map as unhelpfulness
cons.example: an owner who says they hired the operator so they would never have to think about payroll again and resents being asked to approve each run

cons.claim: The map is written against the platform current published division of duties, which the platform can change unilaterally
cons.example: a platform moving a filing class into or out of its agent service and quietly changing who owns it

failure_modes: assuming the platform handles a filing class because it handles the common ones
accepting duties that the operator commercial model does not actually permit
leaving employee-facing questions unassigned so employees call whoever answers first
writing the map once and never reconciling it against a platform service change
acceptance_tests: every duty in the onboarding and recurring lists resolves to exactly one named owner with no duty marked shared
the negatives list is present and includes the operator refusal to sign as an officer of the client or to hold sole agency credentials
revisit_triggers: the platform changes its published service scope or filing coverage
a duty is discovered in production with no owner
the client engages a new adviser or bookkeeper whose scope overlaps the map

nodes.definition: Payroll is a compliance-critical domain in which ordinary-looking configuration choices carry consequence classes that fall on the client: late or short deposits, returns filed for the wrong period, workers reported to the wrong jurisdiction, and statements issued to employees with wrong totals all attract penalty and interest exposure whose amounts and abatement paths are set by the relevant agency and change over time. The operator role is to know which choices carry that weight, to slow down on those and require evidence rather than recollection, and to recognise the question classes that must leave the operator entirely: whether a worker is an employee or a contractor, whether a position is exempt from overtime, how an owner should be paid from their own entity, whether a compensation item is taxable, whether to file an amendment, and how to respond to an agency notice. Those go to the client accountant, tax professional or counsel, in writing, with the facts assembled but no recommendation attached. The discipline is not timidity; it is the difference between an operator whose clients trust the configuration and one who eventually gives an answer that becomes a penalty with the operator name attached to it.

included: the classes of onboarding choice that carry compliance weight
the question classes routed out to a licensed adviser
the written escalation with facts and no recommendation
the rule that specifics are verified in the client jurisdiction rather than recalled
excluded: stating penalty amounts, interest rates or abatement outcomes
giving the tax, legal or accounting answer itself
representing the client before an agency

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an agency notice, penalty assessment or adviser correction on a client file that shows a question class was mishandled

pros.claim: Naming the escalation classes in advance keeps the operator from answering a question that is not theirs under conversational pressure
pros.example: an owner asking on a call whether their spouse can be paid as a contractor gets a written referral to their accountant rather than an opinion

pros.claim: Treating verification as mandatory on high-consequence settings converts vague caution into a repeatable behaviour
pros.example: a deposit frequency is configured from the agency notice in the client file rather than from what the prior provider appeared to be doing

cons.claim: Referral feels like evasion to a client who believed they had hired an expert
cons.example: a small owner with no accountant who hears go ask your adviser and hears nothing useful

cons.claim: Escalation costs project time and can stall a configuration decision that blocks the go-live date
cons.example: waiting on an adviser answer about a fringe benefit while the pay calendar cannot be finalised

failure_modes: answering a classification, exemption or taxability question to keep the conversation moving
repeating a specific rule from memory or from another jurisdiction instead of verifying it currently
escalating verbally so no record exists of what was asked and answered
letting a client treat silence from their adviser as the operator permission to proceed
acceptance_tests: each escalation class has a written trigger and a named destination role, and the client is told at onboarding which questions will always be routed out
every escalation in the file is written, dated, states the facts and contains no operator recommendation
revisit_triggers: a client question arrives that does not fit an existing class
an agency notice or penalty appears on a client account
the client changes or loses their tax adviser

nodes.definition: Onboarding is the one moment when an entire workforce identity set moves in bulk: full legal names, social security numbers, dates of birth, home addresses, wage histories and bank account credentials, plus the client own banking authorization. The protocol governs how that material is asked for, moved, held and destroyed. Intake happens on a channel the client can audit and that is not ordinary email or a chat attachment, ideally by the employees entering their own identifiers and bank details directly into the platform so the operator never holds them. Where a file must be handled, it is minimised to the fields actually required, held only as long as the migration and reconciliation need it, kept out of general working folders, and deleted on a stated schedule with the deletion recorded. Access is least-privilege and time-boxed by role rather than by trust, subcontractors and assistants get the narrowest role that lets them work, and every access is removable in one action when a person leaves or the project ends. The protocol also names the obligation classes that attach to a loss of this data, including client notification duties and jurisdictional breach-notification rules that must be verified currently, and it states plainly that these obligations are why convenience never wins here.

included: intake channel rules and the prefer-self-entry principle
field minimisation, retention window and recorded disposal
least-privilege time-boxed access including subcontractors
the obligation classes attached to a data loss and the duty to verify them currently
excluded: selection and administration of the operator own systems and vendors
the client internal record-keeping obligations as employer
jurisdiction-specific breach-notification specifics, which are verified rather than asserted

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a near-miss or actual exposure of client or employee data, or a change in the platform access model or applicable notification obligations

pros.claim: Employee self-entry removes the largest concentration of identifiers from the operator possession entirely
pros.example: employees enter their own bank details in the platform so no spreadsheet of account numbers ever exists on the operator machine

pros.claim: Time-boxed least-privilege roles make offboarding a person a single revocation rather than an investigation
pros.example: a seasonal assistant loses access to all client companies at project end without anyone reconstructing what they could see

cons.claim: Secure intake is slower and clients push back by sending the roster the easy way anyway
cons.example: an owner attaching a full roster with identifiers to a reply email despite an available secure upload

cons.claim: Aggressive deletion can remove evidence the operator later needs to prove the migration was done correctly
cons.example: a deleted source register that would have settled a dispute about a migrated balance months later

failure_modes: accepting identifiers over ordinary email or chat because the client sent them that way
keeping the migration working file indefinitely in a general folder
granting a helper full administrative access because narrower roles are inconvenient
assuming the platform security posture covers the operator own copies of the same data
acceptance_tests: every sensitive intake in the project arrived on the designated channel, and any that did not is recorded with the remediation taken
each person with access holds the narrowest role that permits their task, with an end date, and the disposal of working copies is recorded on the stated schedule
revisit_triggers: a person joins or leaves the operator side of the engagement
a client sends sensitive data through an unapproved channel
the platform changes its role model or the applicable notification obligations are updated

nodes.definition: Two payroll clients with the same headcount can differ by an order of magnitude in onboarding work, so the first substantive act is to classify what this one actually is. The triage walks a fixed set of complexity drivers and records the answer with evidence rather than with the owner impression: how many jurisdictions the workforce touches, including remote workers whose home address creates a registration question; whether local or municipal taxes are in play; the mix of hourly, salaried, tipped, commissioned and piece-rate pay; whether contractors are paid alongside employees; benefit deductions and their carriers; retirement plan contributions and matching; active garnishment or support orders; unions, certified payroll or prevailing-wage reporting; multiple entities, owners paid from their own company, or a recent entity change; and the state of the prior provider records. Each driver either adds a workstream, adds an agency lead time, or adds an escalation to the client adviser, and the classification is what makes a go-live date honest instead of hopeful. The triage output is also a commercial signal: a client whose complexity exceeds what the operator service layer can carry is better served by saying so before the engagement than by discovering it during migration.

included: the fixed driver checklist and its evidence requirement
translation of drivers into workstreams, lead times and escalations
the honest decline or refer-out when complexity exceeds capability
excluded: resolving any driver, such as deciding a worker classification or a multi-state registration question
pricing the engagement
choosing the platform, which is settled before onboarding starts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a pattern of drivers discovered after triage rather than during it, which adds a question to the checklist

pros.claim: Classifying before committing keeps the date, the scope and the price attached to the real client rather than the imagined one
pros.example: discovering two remote workers in other states during triage rather than during the first tax calculation

pros.claim: A fixed driver list makes junior work reliable because the questions do not depend on who is asking
pros.example: an assistant surfaces an active support order because the checklist asks, not because they knew to ask

cons.claim: Clients under-report complexity in good faith, so the triage is only as accurate as the documents behind it
cons.example: an owner who says everyone is here, forgetting the salesperson who moved away last year

cons.claim: A thorough intake interrogation early can feel like friction to a client who was promised a simple switch
cons.example: a small shop owner impatient with a driver checklist when the prior conversation implied a fast setup

failure_modes: taking headcount as a proxy for complexity
accepting recollection instead of the prior register, the last returns and the deduction schedule
missing a driver with agency lead time so the date collapses later
accepting an engagement whose complexity class the operator cannot actually service
acceptance_tests: every driver on the checklist has a recorded answer with the document or the client written confirmation that supports it
each affirmative driver is mapped to the workstream, lead time or escalation it creates before any date is quoted
revisit_triggers: a new driver appears mid-project, such as a worker in another jurisdiction or a newly served withholding order
the prior-provider records arrive and contradict the intake answers
the client acquires or restructures an entity during onboarding

nodes.definition: The cutover date is the single decision that most changes how much work onboarding contains. A start-of-year cutover means the new system begins with clean accumulators and the prior provider closes out the entire prior year including annual employee statements. A quarter boundary means year-to-date balances still migrate but the periodic returns split cleanly at the boundary, with each provider filing whole periods. A mid-period or mid-quarter cutover means balances migrate, the current period return is split between two systems, and someone must be explicitly assigned to file it correctly, which is the classic source of a return filed twice or not at all. The plan states the chosen boundary, the reason, and the resulting responsibility split in writing agreed by client, prior provider and the new platform, plus the practical constraints: agency authorization lead times, the client funding calendar, and the fact that a business rarely wants its riskiest system change during its busiest week. The operator plans this as an operations decision; when it appears instead as a sales objection about switching pain, that conversation belongs to the acquisition practice.

included: comparison of year, quarter and mid-period cutover classes on migration burden and filing split
written responsibility split for the period containing the cutover
lead-time and business-calendar constraints on the date
excluded: the sales framing of switching pain used to win the client
performing any split-period filing
the recurring filing calendar in production after handoff

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a split-period filing problem traced back to the cutover choice, or a change in what the prior provider will close out

pros.claim: Choosing a clean boundary removes an entire class of split-period filing ambiguity before it can happen
pros.example: a quarter-boundary cutover where each provider files whole periods and nobody has to negotiate who covers a partial one

pros.claim: Writing the responsibility split down converts an assumption into an agreement all three parties can be held to
pros.example: the prior provider confirming in writing that it will produce the annual employee statements for the period it ran

cons.claim: Clean boundaries are scarce, so insisting on one can push a client months out and cost the engagement
cons.example: an urgent switch in the middle of a quarter because the current provider is failing the client now

cons.claim: A year-boundary cutover concentrates every switch into the busiest period, when both providers and the operator have the least capacity
cons.example: a first-of-year go-live competing with annual statement season for the same attention

failure_modes: letting the client set a date without stating what that date adds to the migration
assuming the prior provider will file the split period without written confirmation
choosing a boundary that ignores an agency authorization lead time
cutting over during the client peak trading week
acceptance_tests: the chosen boundary is recorded with the migration consequences it creates, and no consequence is left unassigned
for any period spanning the cutover, a single named party is documented as responsible for each return and each deposit, confirmed by that party
revisit_triggers: an agency authorization or account application misses its expected lead time
the prior provider announces a termination date different from the plan
the client business calendar changes, such as a seasonal peak or an acquisition

nodes.definition: Nothing in payroll happens without authority, and every authority granted is also a liability surface. Onboarding enumerates the classes required and obtains each deliberately: a platform role for the operator that permits configuration and review without becoming the client account owner; the client own owner-level credentials, which stay with the client; third-party access or agent authorization at each tax agency, whose forms, scope and processing time differ by agency and jurisdiction and must be verified currently; banking authorization permitting the platform to debit the funding account and originate payments; and whatever signature authority the platform requires from an officer of the client, which is exercised by the client and never by the operator. Each grant is documented with what it permits, who holds it, when it was given and how it is revoked, and the guiding rule is the narrowest role that performs the task. The common failure is the opposite: an accommodating client hands over owner credentials to save time, which leaves the operator holding an authority they cannot justify, cannot audit, and cannot cleanly hand back at the end of the relationship.

included: the authorization classes required to configure and run payroll
the narrowest-role rule and the documented revocation path
the rule that officer signature authority stays with the client
excluded: jurisdiction-specific authorization forms, scopes and processing times, which are verified currently rather than asserted
the operator internal credential management tooling
the client internal delegation of authority among its own staff

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an agency or platform change to authorization classes, or an access review that finds a grant wider than its task

pros.claim: Explicit narrow grants let the operator work without ever holding authority they cannot defend
pros.example: an operator with a configuration role who can build the company and review a run but cannot approve payment or change the account owner

pros.claim: Documented grants make disengagement clean, which protects both parties whenever the relationship ends
pros.example: a revocation list that lets a departing client remove every operator access in one pass with nothing left behind

cons.claim: Narrow roles create friction in exactly the moments where speed matters most
cons.example: an owner unreachable on payday while an approval waits, because approval authority correctly sits with them

cons.claim: Agency authorization classes carry processing time the project cannot compress
cons.example: an authorization filed on time that is still pending when the first run needs it, forcing an interim arrangement

failure_modes: accepting the client owner-level credentials because it is faster than requesting a proper role
signing or e-signing anything in the capacity of an officer of the client
granting a helper broad access rather than a task role
leaving no record of which grants exist, so none can be revoked reliably
acceptance_tests: each required authorization class has a recorded grant, holder, scope, date and revocation method, and no operator-held grant exceeds the task it serves
the client retains owner-level control of its own platform account and agency credentials, evidenced in the file
revisit_triggers: an agency changes its authorization form, scope or processing path
a person on either side joins or leaves the engagement
the platform changes its role model or introduces a new permission class

nodes.definition: Before a single dollar can be withheld correctly, the client tax identity must exist and be linked. This work unit covers the classes involved: the legal entity name and identification as the agencies hold them, which must match exactly rather than approximately; the federal employer identification; state withholding and state unemployment accounts for every jurisdiction the workforce touches; any local or municipal registrations that apply; the unemployment experience rate as the agency has assigned it; and the deposit frequency each agency has set, which is read off the agency notice rather than inherited from the prior provider configuration or assumed from another client. Each of these is then linked into the platform with the correct account identifiers, and the platform is authorised as filing and payment agent where the client has engaged it in that role. Registrations and authorizations carry agency processing time that no amount of project urgency compresses, so the plan tracks each one from application to confirmation. The operator informs and coordinates; the client, with its adviser, applies for and owns the accounts, and every jurisdictional specific is verified currently rather than remembered.

included: the account and registration classes needed per jurisdiction touched
reading deposit frequency and rate attributes from agency notices
linking accounts into the platform and authorising it as agent where engaged
tracking agency lead times from application to confirmation
excluded: deciding whether a registration is required in a jurisdiction, which is an adviser question
applying on behalf of the client as if the operator were an officer
performing deposits or filings, which the engaged agent or the client performs
any jurisdiction-specific threshold, form or schedule stated as fact rather than verified

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an agency notice, rejection or rate change, or a workforce change that adds a jurisdiction to the account set

pros.claim: Configuring attributes from the agency notice rather than from the prior system stops an inherited error propagating into the new one
pros.example: a deposit frequency the prior provider had set for an earlier year being replaced by the frequency on the current notice

pros.claim: Tracking each registration from application to confirmation converts an invisible dependency into a dated one
pros.example: an unemployment account application whose pending status is visible weeks before it can threaten the go-live date

cons.claim: Agency processing times are outside anyone control and can move the whole project
cons.example: a jurisdiction taking longer than expected to issue an account number, with the first run already scheduled

cons.claim: The number of jurisdictions grows faster than expected once remote work is included, expanding scope after the plan is set
cons.example: a single remote worker adding a whole registration workstream nobody priced

failure_modes: entering the trading name instead of the exact legal name the agency holds
copying deposit frequency or rate from the prior provider configuration
missing a jurisdiction because a remote worker home address was never checked
assuming the platform is authorised as agent for every account when it is authorised for some
acceptance_tests: every jurisdiction the workforce touches has its account identifiers, rate attributes and deposit frequency recorded from an agency source document, and each is entered in the platform and confirmed by the platform validation
for every account, the file records whether the platform is authorised as filing and payment agent and, where it is not, which party performs the deposit and the filing
revisit_triggers: an employee moves or is hired into a new jurisdiction
an agency issues a new rate or frequency notice
a registration application is rejected or returns a different identifier than expected

nodes.definition: A payroll system asks a series of questions whose answers are legal determinations belonging to the employer: is this person an employee or an independent contractor, is this role exempt from overtime, is this owner properly paid through payroll, is this allowance taxable compensation. The system will accept whatever it is told and calculate perfectly on a wrong premise, which is why the boundary matters more here than almost anywhere else in onboarding. The operator practice is to record the client determination as the client states it, to flag the classes that commonly attract scrutiny so the client can take them to their adviser, and to decline to supply the answer, including when the client presses for one because their previous provider always just handled it. The flags are factual and non-directive: this worker is set up as a contractor and is paid on a recurring schedule for work directed by the client, which is a pattern advisers usually want to look at. What follows is the client decision, taken with their adviser, recorded in the file with its date and its source. This preserves both the client right to make its own determination and the operator right to be uninvolved in a mistake it did not make.

included: recording employer determinations as stated with date and source
non-directive flagging of patterns advisers commonly review
the refusal rule and its script
keeping the configuration consistent with the recorded determination
excluded: making or endorsing any classification, exemption or taxability determination
interpreting any classification test or wage and hour rule
advising on how an owner should be compensated from their own entity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a client determination revised by an adviser or challenged by an agency, or a change in how a worker is actually engaged

pros.claim: Recording the determination with its source moves the decision to where the liability already sits
pros.example: a file note that the client accountant confirmed the exempt status of two roles, dated, before payroll was configured

pros.claim: Non-directive flagging gives the client the benefit of the operator pattern recognition without crossing into advice
pros.example: noting that several long-term contractors are paid on the same recurring cycle as staff and suggesting the client raise it with their adviser

cons.claim: Clients experience the refusal as the operator being unhelpful about something obvious
cons.example: an owner who says every provider I have used just told me, and hears a referral instead

cons.claim: Flagging can be heard as an accusation and damage trust early in a relationship
cons.example: a contractor pattern raised in week one landing as a suggestion that the client has been doing something wrong

failure_modes: answering the classification question to keep the setup moving
configuring a worker as the operator believes is correct rather than as the client determined
flagging in a way that implies the answer and becomes advice in substance
leaving the determination undocumented so nobody can show who decided
acceptance_tests: every worker in the system carries a recorded client determination with a date and its source, and no determination originates from the operator
each flagged pattern is recorded factually with the referral made and the client response, whatever that response was
revisit_triggers: a worker role, pay basis or working pattern changes materially
the client adviser revises a prior determination
an agency inquiry touches classification or exempt status

nodes.definition: Before any person is loaded, the rules the system will apply to them are configured: the pay frequency and the actual pay-period calendar with its period start and end dates and its pay dates for the rest of the year, including how a pay date that lands on a weekend or bank holiday is shifted; the processing deadline the platform imposes ahead of each pay date, which is the constraint the client must live inside forever; the pay categories in use, such as regular, overtime, double time, bonus, commission, tips, reimbursement and any category with special tax treatment; the workweek definition that overtime is measured against, as the client has determined it; and the time-off accrual and carryover policy as the client policy document states it, with the platform capability checked against that document rather than the policy quietly reshaped to fit the software. The last point is the frequent trap: a platform accrual model that cannot express the client actual policy is a configuration decision that must be surfaced to the client in writing, not absorbed silently by rounding the policy. Everything here is configuration of employer-decided rules, never a judgement about what the rules should be.

included: pay calendar with period dates, pay dates, holiday shifts and processing deadlines
pay category set and their configured treatment
workweek and overtime measurement as determined by the client
time-off accrual configuration against the written client policy and the gap disclosure when the platform cannot express it
excluded: deciding overtime eligibility, minimum wage compliance or leave entitlement
writing the client time-off policy
the ongoing per-run operating routine after go-live

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a parallel-run variance traced to a pay category or accrual setting, or a client policy change

pros.claim: A published pay calendar with processing deadlines sets an expectation the client can plan cash around from day one
pros.example: an owner who learns during setup that submission closes days before payday rather than discovering it the night before the first run

pros.claim: Checking the accrual policy against platform capability early converts a hidden mismatch into an explicit client decision
pros.example: a carryover rule the platform cannot model, raised in configuration rather than discovered when a balance is wrong

cons.claim: Pay categories multiply and each additional one is another thing that can be mapped wrong in migration
cons.example: separate categories for tips, service charges and bonuses that each need their own tax treatment checked

cons.claim: Configuration cannot fix a client policy that is inconsistent, and surfacing that inconsistency creates work the client did not expect
cons.example: a written policy and an actual practice on carryover that do not match, which the client must reconcile before it can be configured

failure_modes: configuring pay dates without checking holiday and weekend shifts for the rest of the year
silently reshaping the client time-off policy to fit what the platform can express
omitting a pay category that exists in the prior system, so it has nowhere to migrate to
leaving the processing deadline unexplained until the first run is late
acceptance_tests: the pay calendar for the remainder of the year is generated and confirmed by the client, including every shifted pay date and the processing deadline for each
every pay category and accrual rule in the prior system has a configured counterpart or a written note of the difference accepted by the client
revisit_triggers: the client changes pay frequency, workweek or time-off policy
a pay category appears in migration that was not configured
the platform changes its processing deadlines or accrual capabilities

nodes.definition: The roster migration moves each worker from the old system into the new one field class by field class, with a stated source of truth for each: legal name exactly as it appears on the identity record rather than the name people use day to day; identifier and date of birth; the home address that drives residence taxation and the work location that drives the employment jurisdiction, which are distinct fields that a remote worker makes obviously different; hire date and rehire history, which drive eligibility and reporting; pay rate and pay basis; scheduled hours where they matter; withholding elections as the employee has actually filed them, which are re-collected from the employee rather than copied blindly when the prior data is unreliable or the form generation has changed; status, including terminated workers who must still appear because they have year-to-date balances and will need annual statements; and the internal identifiers that let the old and new records be matched during reconciliation. Every field gets a validation rule, because the errors here are silent: a transposed identifier does not stop a payroll, it produces a statement that will not match agency records, and a work location left as the office address quietly taxes a remote worker in the wrong jurisdiction for months.

included: field-class mapping from the prior register or export with a source of truth per field
validation rules that catch silent errors
inclusion of terminated workers with balances
re-collection of withholding elections where the source data cannot be trusted
excluded: year-to-date balances, which migrate as their own controlled workstream
deduction and benefit setup
deciding a worker classification or exempt status

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an employee-reported data error or a reconciliation difference that reveals a field mapped from the wrong source

pros.claim: Field-level sourcing prevents the quiet errors that only surface at annual statement time
pros.example: separating home address from work location so a remote worker is not taxed to the office jurisdiction all year

pros.claim: Carrying terminated workers with balances across avoids a year-end scramble to produce statements the system has no data for
pros.example: two workers who left mid-year loaded with their balances so their annual statements come out of the new system correctly

cons.claim: Re-collecting elections and details from employees adds a dependency on people who do not answer promptly
cons.example: a handful of employees who never complete their self-onboarding invitation while the go-live date approaches

cons.claim: Prior-system exports are frequently incomplete or structured for the old platform assumptions, so mapping is judgement work
cons.example: an export with a single combined name field and no separate work location, which has to be rebuilt from other records

failure_modes: loading the day-to-day name rather than the legal name on the identity record
defaulting work location to the company address for every worker
excluding terminated workers and losing their balances and statements
copying withholding elections from an unreliable export instead of re-collecting them
acceptance_tests: every migrated record passes its field validations, and every exception is listed with the correction or the client written confirmation of the value
the count and identity of workers in the new system reconcile to the prior register, including terminated workers with balances, with any difference explained
revisit_triggers: an employee reports a wrong name, address or election after go-live
a parallel-run variance points at a roster field rather than a rule
the prior provider supplies a corrected or more complete export

nodes.definition: Everything that comes out of a paycheck other than tax has to be rebuilt deliberately, because each item carries three attributes that migrate independently: the amount or formula, the tax treatment, and the party who remits it. Pre-tax classes such as certain health premiums and retirement contributions reduce taxable wages and therefore change tax calculations if their treatment is set wrong; post-tax classes do not. Employer contributions and matching formulas are configured alongside the employee side because both flow into the accumulators. Carrier and provider arrangements decide whether the platform sends a payment, produces a report, or does nothing while the client pays the carrier directly, and that owner must be named per item rather than assumed. Court, agency and support withholding orders are a different species entirely: they are legal instruments served on the employer, they carry their own calculation rules, priorities and limits, they continue across a provider change without pausing, and the remittance destination and reference matter as much as the amount. Onboarding treats an active order as a first-class migration item with its own evidence, its own continuity check across the cutover, and an explicit rule that questions about how an order should be applied go to the client adviser or the issuing authority rather than being answered by the operator.

included: pre-tax and post-tax deduction classes with their configured treatment
employer contribution and match configuration
named remitter per item
active withholding orders as evidenced legal instruments with a continuity check across cutover
excluded: interpreting an order, its priority or its limits, which belongs to the client adviser or the issuing authority
benefit plan design, eligibility and carrier brokerage
the recurring remittance routine after go-live

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new or amended order, a carrier arrangement change, or a variance showing a treatment configured against the plan document

pros.claim: Separating amount, tax treatment and remitter stops the most common silent migration defect in this area
pros.example: a premium migrated as post-tax when the client plan treats it as pre-tax, caught because treatment is migrated as its own attribute

pros.claim: Treating an active order as a first-class item with a continuity check protects both the employee and the client from a missed statutory withholding
pros.example: a support order verified as withheld and remitted on the first run after cutover with the same reference the issuing authority expects

cons.claim: The information lives in several places and no single export contains it, so assembly is slow
cons.example: premium amounts in a carrier invoice, treatment in the plan document, and the order itself in a paper file in the owner desk

cons.claim: Migration cannot resolve an ambiguous order, and waiting on the issuing authority can outlast the go-live date
cons.example: an order whose remittance instructions are unclear, where the answer must come from the authority rather than from the operator

failure_modes: migrating an amount without its tax treatment
assuming the platform remits a carrier payment it does not remit
letting a withholding order lapse for a period because the migration was in progress
interpreting an order calculation rule rather than routing the question
acceptance_tests: every deduction, contribution and match in the prior system exists in the new one with amount, treatment and named remitter recorded, and any dropped item is confirmed in writing by the client
every active withholding order is evidenced in the file and verified as withheld and remitted correctly on the first run after cutover, with no gap period
revisit_triggers: a new order is served or an existing one is amended or released
a carrier changes plan terms, rates or remittance arrangements
an employee changes benefit elections during the migration window

nodes.definition: A mid-year cutover only works if the new system starts with the year already accumulated inside it, because payroll arithmetic is cumulative: wage-base-limited taxes stop at a threshold, annual contribution limits apply across the year regardless of who processed it, and annual employee statements must cover the whole year from one place. The migration loads the accumulator classes per employee and per employer, including gross wages by category, each withheld tax by jurisdiction, each employer tax, employer and employee contribution totals, and every deduction accumulator, using evidenced source documents rather than a summary someone typed: the prior provider payroll registers for the year, the periodic returns already filed, and the deposit records. The rule that keeps this honest is that a balance is not migrated because it was provided; it is migrated because it ties to a filed return or a register, and any figure that does not tie is quarantined and resolved before it is loaded. Terminated employees are loaded too. This is the single highest-consequence data movement in onboarding, because a wrong balance does not fail loudly on the next run; it silently produces wrong withholding for the remainder of the year and a wrong annual statement at the end of it.

included: accumulator classes loaded per employee and per employer
evidenced source documents and the tie-out rule before loading
terminated employees with balances
quarantine and resolution of untied figures
excluded: the reconciliation to filed returns, which is its own verification unit
amending anything already filed by the prior provider
the annual statement production process itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a corrected prior-provider register, an amended return, or any later period that fails to tie to the loaded balances

pros.claim: Loading only tied balances stops a prior-system error being inherited and compounded for the rest of the year
pros.example: a wage-base-limited tax that would have restarted from zero after cutover, caught because the balance did not tie to the filed return

pros.claim: Complete accumulators let the new system produce the annual statements alone, removing a dependency on a provider the client has left
pros.example: year-end statements produced entirely from the new system rather than assembled from two partial sets

cons.claim: The work depends on records held by the outgoing provider, whose cooperation and timeliness cannot be assumed
cons.example: a final register that arrives only after repeated requests, compressing the reconciliation window

cons.claim: Accumulator structures differ between platforms, so some mapping is judgement rather than transcription
cons.example: a prior system that combined categories the new one keeps separate, requiring a documented apportionment

failure_modes: loading balances from a summary that nobody tied to a filed return
omitting employer-side accumulators because only employee figures were checked
leaving terminated employees out of the load
loading a partial period twice because the cutover boundary was not applied consistently
acceptance_tests: every loaded accumulator ties to a register, a filed return or a deposit record, with the source cited, and untied figures are quarantined rather than loaded
the loaded totals are re-extracted from the new system after loading and compared back to the source, employee by employee, with zero unexplained difference
revisit_triggers: the prior provider issues a corrected register or an amended return
a parallel run or first live run shows a tax stopping or continuing at the wrong point
an employee statement or periodic return does not tie at the next boundary

nodes.definition: A payroll that calculates perfectly and does not pay anybody is a failed payroll, so the money chain is set up and tested as its own workstream. On the employee side, account and routing details are captured, preferably entered by employees themselves so the operator never holds them, and verified by whatever method the platform and bank support before payday depends on them; split deposits and any employees who remain on paper payment are recorded deliberately rather than by omission. On the company side, the funding account is authorised for debit, the platform funding deadline and the cutoff time are established, and the client is told in plain terms how many days before payday money must be available and what happens if it is not. The lead time for verification and for the first debit is longer than clients expect and is often the true constraint on the go-live date. This unit also carries a permanent anti-fraud rule that starts at onboarding: a request to change bank details, from an employee or purportedly from the owner, is verified out of band on a known contact before it is actioned, no matter how ordinary the request looks, because payroll redirection is a standard fraud against exactly this data.

included: employee account capture, self-entry preference and verification
company funding account authorization, funding deadline and cutoff
deliberate handling of split deposits and non-electronic payment
out-of-band verification rule for any bank-detail change
excluded: the client cash management and whether it can fund a given run
banking rails and platform payment engineering
the ongoing funding routine after go-live

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a returned or misdirected payment, an attempted redirection request, or a platform change to funding timing or verification

pros.claim: Verified accounts and a tested debit turn the first payday from a hope into a checked chain
pros.example: a company debit tested ahead of the first run so a wrong account number surfaces before employees are waiting on money

pros.claim: An out-of-band verification rule set at onboarding blocks the most common fraud aimed at payroll
pros.example: an emailed request to redirect an employee deposit that is confirmed by phone on a known number and turns out to be false

cons.claim: Verification lead times are rigid and often decide the go-live date rather than the other way around
cons.example: account verification still in progress when the client wanted to run payroll that week

cons.claim: Employee self-entry depends on employees acting, and some will not act in time
cons.example: a worker who never completes their bank entry and must be paid by another method for the first run

failure_modes: going live with unverified employee accounts
leaving the client unaware of the funding deadline until the first run is late
actioning a bank-detail change from an inbound message without out-of-band verification
forgetting the employees who were paid by another method in the old system
acceptance_tests: every employee payment method is recorded and verified by the platform supported method before the first live run, with any unverified worker on a documented alternate payment path
the company funding authorization is in place and the funding deadline and cutoff are confirmed in writing by the client, with a tested debit or platform equivalent before go-live
revisit_triggers: any request to change employee or company bank details
a failed, returned or delayed transfer
the platform changes funding deadlines, cutoffs or verification methods

nodes.definition: The people most exposed to a payroll migration are the ones with no say in it, and they judge the whole change by whether their pay arrives on time and looks right. The communication is short, factual and sent in the employer voice rather than the operator voice, because it is the employer relationship with its staff: what is changing and on which pay date, that pay amounts and pay dates are not changing unless the employer separately says so, what each person must do and by when (typically completing a self-onboarding invitation and re-entering or confirming bank details and withholding elections), where their pay statements will live afterwards and how to reach the historical ones, and who to ask if something looks wrong, which is a named person on the client side. Two prohibitions are absolute: the announcement never travels with personal data attached, and it never asks anyone to send identifiers or bank details by reply, because that is precisely the message a fraudster imitates. Handled well this is a quiet non-event; handled badly it produces a week of anxious employees, a flood of questions the client is not ready for, and a first payday people were already braced to distrust.

included: announcement content, timing and employer voice
the employee task list and its deadline
access to historical and future pay statements
the prohibition on personal data or credential requests travelling in the message
excluded: any statement about pay amounts, benefits or employment terms, which are the employer to make
employee tax questions, which are routed to the employer or an adviser
ongoing employee support after go-live

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: employee confusion, low task completion or a reported phishing attempt following the announcement

pros.claim: A clear employer-voice message converts a switch employees would otherwise notice as a disruption into an administrative non-event
pros.example: staff who complete their self-onboarding in the first week because the message came from their own manager with a date

pros.claim: Stating that nobody will be asked for bank details by reply inoculates the workforce against the fraud the transition invites
pros.example: an employee forwarding a suspicious payroll email to the client contact instead of answering it

cons.claim: The message is outside the operator control and clients often send nothing, or send it too late to matter
cons.example: a client who forgets to announce the change until employees start asking why they got an invitation from an unfamiliar system

cons.claim: Announcing early increases the volume of employee questions during the busiest configuration week
cons.example: a wave of questions about pay statements arriving while the migration reconciliation is still open

failure_modes: sending the announcement in the operator voice so employees think an outside party now handles their pay
attaching a roster or any personal data to a broadcast message
asking employees to reply with identifiers or bank details
omitting how to reach historical pay statements after the old system access ends
acceptance_tests: the announcement is sent by the client before the first live run, names a client-side contact, states the employee task and its deadline, and contains no personal data and no request for identifiers or bank details by reply
employee task completion is tracked, and every worker who has not completed theirs before the readiness gate has a documented fallback
revisit_triggers: employee task completion stalls before the gate
employees report a suspicious message referencing the payroll change
the client changes the announced first pay date

nodes.definition: The parallel run is the proof that the configuration is right, and it works because it compares the new system against an answer that is already known and already paid. A recent pay period that the prior system produced is re-entered into the new configuration and calculated without paying anything, then compared line by line: gross by category, each withheld tax, each employer tax, each deduction and contribution, and net pay, for every employee rather than a sample. The passing standard is not close enough; it is that every variance is explained by a named cause, and the two acceptable causes are a deliberate configuration change the client has approved and a demonstrable error in the prior system that the client has been told about. Everything else is an unexplained variance and blocks cutover until it resolves. Two disciplines make it real: compare at the line level rather than on net, because offsetting errors cancel out and hide, and run enough periods or enough employee types to exercise the unusual cases such as overtime, a bonus, a wage-base threshold crossing and an active withholding order. The parallel run is also where migration errors are still cheap, which is exactly why it must not be the step that gets compressed when the date is tight.

included: recomputation of an already-paid period without payment
line-level comparison across all employees and pay categories
the explain-every-variance standard and its two acceptable causes
coverage of unusual cases such as thresholds, bonuses and withholding orders
excluded: reconciliation of year-to-date balances to filed returns, which is its own control
paying anything or transmitting any live filing
correcting the prior system errors it uncovers, which is the client decision with its adviser

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a first-live-run error of a class the parallel run should have caught, which extends the coverage rule

pros.claim: Comparing against an already-paid period turns configuration correctness into an objective test rather than a review opinion
pros.example: a mis-set overtime multiplier that appears as a variance on two employees instead of surfacing on the first real payday

pros.claim: The run frequently uncovers errors the prior system was making, which the client can then take to their adviser
pros.example: a deduction that had been treated as pre-tax in the old system contrary to the plan document, surfaced as a variance

cons.claim: It is real effort on a project already under date pressure, and it is the first thing a client asks to skip
cons.example: an owner arguing the platform is well known so a test run is unnecessary

cons.claim: A variance can be caused by the prior system being wrong, which turns a technical check into a delicate client conversation
cons.example: having to tell a client their previous provider had been withholding a benefit incorrectly all year

failure_modes: comparing only net pay so offsetting errors pass
sampling a few simple employees and missing every unusual case
accepting small variances as rounding without identifying the cause
running the comparison after cutover, when errors are expensive rather than free
acceptance_tests: the comparison covers every employee and every pay category at the line level for at least one already-paid period, including at least one period containing an unusual case where the client has any
every variance is closed with a named cause and a client-approved disposition, with zero unexplained variances remaining before cutover
revisit_triggers: any configuration change made after the parallel run passes
a new pay category, deduction or order appears before cutover
the prior provider issues a corrected register for the compared period

nodes.definition: The parallel run proves the calculation rules; this control proves the history. Every migrated accumulator is tied back to what has already been reported to the agencies for the year: the periodic returns filed by the prior provider, the deposit records behind them, and the register totals underneath both. The reconciliation is done per jurisdiction and per tax class rather than in aggregate, because a total can tie while two jurisdictions are individually wrong, and it is documented as a worksheet showing source, loaded value and difference. Differences are worked to a named cause, and the outcome classes are distinct: a migration mapping error, which the operator fixes; a prior-provider reporting error, which belongs to the client and its adviser to decide whether and how to correct; or a timing difference at the cutover boundary, which must be explained rather than absorbed. Nothing is netted off or plugged. This is the control that decides whether the coming annual statements and the next periodic return will tie, and discovering a discrepancy here, while the prior provider still answers the phone and the period is still open, is the difference between a correction and an amendment.

included: per-jurisdiction and per-tax-class tie-out of migrated balances to filed returns and deposits
documented worksheet with source, loaded value and difference
classification of each difference into migration error, prior-provider error or boundary timing
excluded: preparing or filing any amendment, which belongs to the client and its adviser or the engaged agent
advising whether an identified prior-period error should be corrected
the ongoing periodic reconciliation performed after handoff

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an agency notice, an amended return, or a later period that does not tie, each of which reopens the worksheet

pros.claim: Tying to filed returns is the only check that proves the new system agrees with what agencies already believe
pros.example: a jurisdiction whose loaded withholding is short of the filed return, found while the prior provider can still explain it

pros.claim: Classifying each difference by cause routes it to the party who can actually act on it
pros.example: a prior-period reporting error handed to the client accountant with the worksheet rather than quietly adjusted in the new system

cons.claim: It depends on documents the client may never have collected and the prior provider may release slowly
cons.example: filed returns the owner has never seen because the provider filed them without sending copies

cons.claim: Finding a prior-provider error creates an unwelcome conversation and work the client did not budget for
cons.example: a discrepancy that implies an amendment the client must pay their accountant to handle

failure_modes: reconciling in aggregate so offsetting jurisdictional errors cancel
plugging a difference into an adjustment account to make the totals agree
accepting balances that were never compared to a filed return
deferring the reconciliation until after the prior provider relationship has ended
acceptance_tests: a worksheet exists per jurisdiction and tax class showing filed-return source, loaded value and difference, with every non-zero difference assigned a cause class and an owner
no difference is closed by adjustment without a documented cause, and any prior-period issue is referred in writing to the client and its adviser
revisit_triggers: an amended return or corrected register is issued for the period
an agency notice arrives concerning a period covered by the reconciliation
the next periodic return fails to tie to the balances

nodes.definition: The readiness gate is a single decision point with a written checklist and one rule: everything is green or the date moves. The checklist covers the accounts and authorizations confirmed active rather than merely applied for; the roster validated and every exception closed; the balances loaded, re-extracted and tied to filed returns; deductions, contributions and active withholding orders configured and evidenced; employee payment methods verified and the company funding chain tested with the funding deadline confirmed; the pay calendar published; the parallel run closed with zero unexplained variances; the employee announcement sent and the task completion tracked; the split-period filing responsibility agreed in writing with the outgoing provider; and a named contingency if the first run fails, which for most small clients means the ability to pay by another method rather than not at all. The gate is deliberately unpleasant to override, because every incentive in the project pushes toward going live anyway: the client has told employees, the prior provider has been given notice, and the operator wants to invoice. The professional position is that a moved date costs a conversation and a missed payday costs the relationship, so the gate holds and the reason for any override is written down and owned by the client in writing.

included: the written pass conditions across accounts, data, money, verification and communication
the authority to move the go-live date
the contingency plan for a failed first run
the written client-owned record of any override
excluded: performing the first live run itself
renegotiating the commercial terms of the engagement
the ongoing per-run approval routine after handoff

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a first live run that failed on something the checklist did not cover, which adds an item to the gate

pros.claim: One explicit gate replaces a dozen implicit assumptions that the project is ready
pros.example: a checklist that catches an unconfirmed agency authorization nobody had revisited since it was applied for

pros.claim: A written override with client ownership makes proceeding on an amber item a conscious, attributable decision
pros.example: a client who chooses to go live with one unverified employee account and accepts the alternate payment path in writing

cons.claim: A hard gate late in the project produces its most painful conversation at its worst moment
cons.example: telling a client the week before their announced first payday that the date must move

cons.claim: Rigid all-green criteria can block a launch over an item whose risk is genuinely immaterial
cons.example: a single terminated employee record with a trivial discrepancy holding an otherwise ready client

failure_modes: treating the gate as a status meeting rather than a decision with a written outcome
marking items green on assurance instead of evidence
overriding verbally so no record shows who accepted the risk
having no contingency for a first run that fails
acceptance_tests: every checklist item has an evidence reference and a green marking before the first live run is scheduled, and no item is green on verbal assurance alone
any override is recorded with the item, the risk, the mitigation and the client written acceptance, and the contingency payment path is named and workable
revisit_triggers: any configuration or data change after the gate is passed
an authorization or verification that lapses or is withdrawn before the run
the client changes the first pay date after the gate

nodes.definition: The old provider does not simply stop; it must be exited in a controlled sequence, and the two ways this goes wrong are opposite and equally bad. A gap leaves a deposit or a return that neither provider files. A duplicate leaves both providers filing the same period, which is often harder to unwind than a miss. The exit therefore fixes in writing what the outgoing provider will still do after the last run it processes, which typically includes the deposits and returns for periods it ran and, where the cutover is at a year boundary, the annual employee statements; what it will not do; and the date its authority on each agency account ends, which must be sequenced against the new agent authorization starting so the account is never claimed by two agents or by none. Before access ends, everything the client will ever need is retrieved and stored on the client side: full payroll registers for the period, filed returns and deposit confirmations, employee documents, and the accumulator detail behind the migration. Termination is scheduled only after the readiness gate is green, because a provider cancelled early while the new system is not ready leaves a client with no way to pay anyone. The service agreement and any notice period are the client to manage; the operator supplies the sequence and the retrieval list.

included: written split of post-cutover obligations with the outgoing provider
sequencing of agent authority ending and starting per agency account
retrieval and client-side storage of registers, returns, deposit records and employee documents
termination scheduled only after the readiness gate is green
excluded: negotiating the client contract, notice period or fees with the outgoing provider
filing anything for the pre-cutover period
any dispute between the client and the outgoing provider

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an agency notice showing a missing or duplicated filing at the boundary, or a change in what the outgoing provider commits to complete

pros.claim: A written split removes the gap-or-duplicate risk at the boundary where it always occurs
pros.example: the outgoing provider confirming in writing which final deposits and return it will still make after its last processed run

pros.claim: Retrieving records before access ends preserves the only evidence that can settle a later question
pros.example: the full year registers downloaded before the account closes, which later resolves an employee query about a mid-year balance

cons.claim: The outgoing provider has no incentive to be prompt or generous with a departing client
cons.example: record requests answered slowly or partially once cancellation notice has been given

cons.claim: Running two providers until the gate is green costs the client duplicate fees for a period
cons.example: an overlapping month of fees a cost-conscious owner resists paying

failure_modes: cancelling the old provider before the new system is verified ready
assuming the outgoing provider will file the final period without written confirmation
letting both providers hold agent authority on the same account into the same period
losing access to registers and filed returns before they were retrieved
acceptance_tests: a written statement from the outgoing provider lists the final deposits, returns and statements it will produce and the date its authority ends on each account, with no period unassigned and none assigned twice
the full record set for the year is retrieved and stored on the client side before access ends, and the retrieval is recorded in the onboarding file
revisit_triggers: the outgoing provider changes its stated final obligations or termination date
an agency shows two agents or no agent on an account
a record is found missing after access has ended

nodes.definition: The first live run is supervised rather than merely processed, and the supervision extends past the moment the run is approved. Before approval the operator reviews the preview against expectation: headcount and who is being paid, gross by category compared with the parallel-run baseline, every tax present that should be present for each jurisdiction, deductions and active withholding orders applied, net pay outliers examined individually, and the total funding requirement compared with what the client is expecting to be debited. Approval itself is the client act, because the employer approves its own payroll. After approval the supervision continues into the parts that fail silently: confirming the debit cleared, confirming the payments were transmitted and that no employee payment was returned, confirming the tax liabilities were accrued and, where the platform is engaged as agent, that the deposit was made on the agency schedule.
