The first run is scheduled with slack ahead of the actual pay date wherever the platform allows, so a failure has somewhere to go, and the operator is genuinely reachable that day rather than nominally available.

included: pre-approval review against the parallel-run baseline and expectation
the client approval act
post-run confirmation of debit, transmission, returns and tax accrual or deposit
scheduling slack and operator availability on the day
excluded: approving payroll on behalf of the client
the steady-state per-run routine that the recurring practice operates afterwards
correcting an error, which has its own paths

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any first-run failure and its cause, which adds a check to the pre-approval review or the post-run confirmation list

pros.claim: Reviewing before approval catches the class of error that a report after the fact can only document
pros.example: a missing jurisdiction tax on one remote employee spotted in the preview rather than in a later notice

pros.claim: Post-run confirmation catches the failures that never announce themselves
pros.example: a single returned employee deposit discovered and re-paid the same day instead of found when the employee calls

cons.claim: Supervision is time-expensive at exactly the moment the operator is running several onboardings
cons.example: two clients whose first runs land in the same week, both needing the same undivided attention

cons.claim: Close supervision can create an expectation that every run will be reviewed at that depth forever
cons.example: a client who assumes the hypercare review is the permanent service level and is surprised by the steady-state routine

failure_modes: approving the run on the client behalf to save time
reviewing only the totals rather than per-employee and per-jurisdiction detail
treating a successfully submitted run as a successfully paid run
scheduling the first run so tight to the pay date that nothing can be repaired
acceptance_tests: the pre-approval review is documented against the parallel-run baseline with every outlier explained, and approval is recorded as the client act
post-run confirmations are recorded for the company debit, employee payment transmission and returns, and the tax accrual or deposit, before the run is considered closed
revisit_triggers: any returned payment, failed debit or missed deposit on the run
a variance from the parallel-run baseline that has no explanation
an employee reports a pay discrepancy after the run

nodes.definition: Errors in the first weeks after cutover are ordinary, and the practice that matters is knowing which repair class applies and how fast its window closes. The classes are distinct: an underpayment or missed worker is usually repaired with an off-cycle run, which itself has funding and timing consequences; a payment sent to a wrong account may be recoverable only inside a short reversal window that the platform and the bank define, and outside it becomes a recovery conversation between employer and employee rather than a systems action; a wrong tax configuration caught before a deposit is a configuration fix, while the same error after a deposit or a return becomes a correction or amendment involving the agency, with any penalty and interest exposure and any abatement request being the client matter with its adviser; an overpayment is a legal and policy question about recovery that belongs to the employer and its counsel, not to the operator. The operator work is triage and evidence: identify the class immediately because windows are short, tell the client plainly and quickly rather than after investigating alone, document what happened and when, and route every filing, penalty and recovery decision to the party that owns it. Speed and candour do more to preserve the relationship here than a perfect explanation delivered late.

included: identification of the repair class and its window
the immediate disclosure rule to the client
evidence capture of what happened and when
routing of filing, penalty and recovery decisions to their owner
excluded: preparing or filing amendments and penalty or abatement correspondence
deciding whether to pursue recovery of an overpayment
advising on penalty exposure or its likely outcome

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new incident class, an agency response to a correction, or a platform change to its correction windows

pros.claim: Classifying the repair immediately preserves the short windows that only exist for hours or days
pros.example: a misdirected payment escalated inside the reversal window rather than after it, when only a recovery conversation remains

pros.claim: Disclosing quickly and plainly is what actually keeps the client, because the error will surface regardless
pros.example: the operator calling the owner the same morning with the facts and the plan rather than the owner hearing it from an employee

cons.claim: Disclosure invites blame and can cost the relationship even when the error originated elsewhere
cons.example: a client attributing a prior-provider balance error to the migration because the migration is what changed

cons.claim: Repairs consume unbilled operator time and often arrive at the worst point in the schedule
cons.example: an off-cycle run and its reconciliation landing in the same week as another client cutover

failure_modes: investigating quietly while a reversal or correction window closes
handling a post-deposit error as if it were a simple configuration fix
advising the client on penalty exposure or abatement instead of routing it
leaving no dated record of the error, the notification and the repair
acceptance_tests: each incident is recorded with its class, the window that applied, the time the client was notified and the action taken, with notification preceding investigation completion
every agency filing, penalty and recovery decision arising from an incident is documented as routed to the client and its adviser or the engaged agent rather than decided by the operator
revisit_triggers: any post-cutover error of a class not previously encountered
an agency notice or penalty assessment arrives
a platform change to reversal, void or off-cycle capabilities and their windows

nodes.definition: Onboarding ends by converting the service boundary map into a dated calendar the client and the ongoing service can both operate from. Each recurring obligation class appears as a line with its cadence, its owner and what evidence proves it was done: the per-run submission deadline and funding requirement; the tax deposit cadence per agency as that agency has assigned it; periodic returns; annual employee statements and their distribution; contractor reporting where relevant; new-hire reporting; the rate and frequency notices that arrive and must be actioned when they do; and any client-specific item such as a benefit remittance or a withholding order review. Every line names one owner from the boundary map, and the calendar states plainly which lines the platform performs as agent, which the client performs, and which the operator watches. This is a handoff artifact, not an operating manual: it is built during onboarding and then run by the recurring service practice, whose per-run rhythm, triage and expansion work sit outside this project. Building it at the end while the configuration is fresh is what stops the first quarter after go-live from becoming a set of surprises nobody had a date for.

included: the obligation-class calendar with cadence, owner and evidence per line
explicit marking of platform-as-agent versus client-performed lines
client-specific recurring items discovered during onboarding
the handoff conversation that transfers the calendar to the recurring practice
excluded: operating the calendar after handoff, including the per-run routine and period-end execution
jurisdiction-specific due dates asserted as fact rather than read from the agency or platform source
issue triage and escalation once the relationship is in production

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an agency cadence change, a new client obligation, or a missed obligation in the first periods after handoff

pros.claim: A calendar with an owner per line converts the boundary map from a principle into something someone can be held to on a date
pros.example: the line for acting on an annual rate notice carrying a named owner instead of being an assumption

pros.claim: Building it while configuration knowledge is fresh captures the client-specific items that would otherwise be forgotten
pros.example: a monthly benefit remittance that only exists for this client landing on the calendar during handoff

cons.claim: A calendar can create a false sense of coverage if its lines are generic rather than derived from this client accounts
cons.example: a template calendar that omits a local jurisdiction registration this client actually holds

cons.claim: Dates and cadences change by agency action, so the calendar decays and needs an owner for its own maintenance
cons.example: a deposit frequency reassigned by an agency notice partway through the year

failure_modes: issuing a generic calendar not derived from the client actual accounts and configuration
leaving lines with a shared or unnamed owner
asserting due dates from memory rather than from the agency or platform source
handing the calendar over without a conversation, so the receiving side never adopts it
acceptance_tests: every obligation line derives from an account, configuration item or order in this client file, and each carries a cadence, exactly one named owner and the evidence that proves completion
the handoff to the client and to the ongoing service is acknowledged in writing, with the maintenance owner for the calendar itself named
revisit_triggers: an agency changes a cadence or issues a new notice
the client adds a jurisdiction, benefit or order
the platform changes which obligations it performs as agent

nodes.definition: The project closes on an evidence file and a signature, because months later the only thing that settles a question about what was configured, who decided it and what was verified is the record. The file assembles what already exists rather than creating new paperwork: the engagement frame and dependency register with its dated changes, the service boundary map, the authorization grants and their revocation methods, the recorded employer determinations with their sources, the configuration record for pay rules and deductions, the roster validation exceptions and their dispositions, the balance load with its source citations, the reconciliation worksheet, the parallel-run variance log with dispositions, the readiness gate with any written override, the outgoing provider written close-out, the first-run supervision record, any incident and its repair, and the compliance calendar with its acknowledgement. The client signs off that the configuration reflects its determinations and that onboarding is complete, which both closes the project commercially and marks the point where the service becomes the recurring relationship. Retention obeys the confidentiality protocol, so the file keeps evidence rather than hoarding raw identifier sets, and access to it stays least-privilege after the project ends.

included: assembly of the evidence artifacts produced during the project
the client sign-off that closes onboarding
retention and access rules applied to the file itself
the marker that transitions the engagement into the recurring relationship
excluded: the client own statutory record-keeping obligations as employer, which have their own retention classes to verify
storing raw identifier or credential sets beyond what evidence requires
post-handoff service documentation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a dispute the file could not answer, or a change in retention obligations that alters what the file may hold

pros.claim: An assembled evidence file answers later questions with a record instead of a recollection
pros.example: a query about why a deduction was configured as it was, answered from the dated determination and its source

pros.claim: A sign-off gives the project a defined end, which protects both the operator scope and the client expectation
pros.example: the client acknowledging completion so later configuration requests are handled as service rather than unfinished onboarding

cons.claim: Assembly is administrative work at the moment everyone considers the project already over
cons.example: a client who has moved on and will not sign anything once the first payroll ran cleanly

cons.claim: The file concentrates sensitive material, so it becomes something that must itself be protected and eventually disposed of
cons.example: reconciliation worksheets containing wage detail that must be retained under access control rather than left in a project folder

failure_modes: closing the project with no signed acknowledgement, leaving scope open indefinitely
keeping raw identifier and bank data in the file because it was convenient
assembling the file from memory after the fact rather than from artifacts produced along the way
leaving broad access to the file after the project team disperses
acceptance_tests: every artifact named in the file index exists, is dated, and is traceable to the work unit that produced it, with no gap in the required set
the client sign-off is recorded, and the file contents and access comply with the retention and least-privilege rules of the confidentiality protocol
revisit_triggers: a dispute or query arises about what was configured or decided
the retention window on an artifact class expires
the engagement scope changes after handoff

edges.why_related: the triage is the first substantive act inside the frame and supplies the complexity class the plan and the date are built from
the frame lists the duties that exist in the project, and the map is what assigns each of them to a party
the escalation classes define the duties that leave the three-party map entirely and go to a licensed adviser
the drivers found in triage determine how costly each cutover boundary is and which lead times constrain the date
least-privilege and time-boxing are the principles that decide which role is requested for each grant
classification, exemption and taxability are the escalation classes made concrete at the point the system asks for them
agency accounts cannot be linked or worked without the authorization class that permits access and agent action
overtime measurement and pay category treatment follow the exempt and classification determinations the client has made
the roster move is the bulk transfer the protocol exists to govern, including the preference for employee self-entry
workers are loaded against pay categories, calendars and accrual rules that must already exist to receive them
deductions, contributions and withholding orders attach to worker records that must already be loaded and validated
payment methods are captured and verified per worker record, so the roster is the prerequisite for the money chain
accumulators load onto identified worker records, including terminated workers who must exist before their balances can
recomputing a paid period only reproduces the prior result if the accumulators behind wage bases and limits are already right
the reconciliation is the proof step for exactly the balances the migration loaded
a closed variance log with no unexplained items is one of the gate pass conditions
the gate cannot be green while any migrated balance is untied to what has already been reported to an agency
the gate is the authorisation to schedule and run the first live payroll at all
the announcement tells employees what to do about their own payment details, so the payment setup must exist before it is sent
the calendar is built once the configuration has actually produced a payroll, so its lines reflect what really happens
the acknowledged calendar is the last artifact the closing file assembles before sign-off
bank credentials are the most attractive data in the project, so the protocol constrains how they may be collected, held and changed
no worker may be loaded under a classification the operator supplied; the migration may only implement a recorded client determination
amendment, penalty and abatement decisions are escalation classes, so the repair paths are constrained to triage and evidence rather than decision
every calendar line must carry exactly one owner drawn from the map, so the map constrains what a valid calendar looks like
the clean boundary that minimises migration and filing risk is frequently not the date the client wants, and the frame carries the client date
edges.resolution_rule: state the added migration and split-filing work each earlier date creates and let the client choose in writing; where the client chooses the earlier date, the added work is added to the plan and the register rather than absorbed silently, and no verification step is dropped to fund it

edges.why_related: verification consumes exactly the days the announced go-live date has already spent
edges.resolution_rule: verification depth is fixed and the date moves; compressing the parallel run or the reconciliation is never the way a schedule is recovered, and any client decision to proceed on an open variance is recorded as a written override at the gate

edges.why_related: clients routinely offer wider authority than the operator role permits because it is faster than arranging the correct grant
edges.resolution_rule: the boundary map wins: take the narrowest grant that performs the task, decline owner-level credentials and officer signature authority, and if the correct grant is unavailable the task waits or moves to the client rather than the role expanding

edges.why_related: a smooth transition invites putting useful personal detail in front of employees, which is exactly what the protocol forbids in a broadcast
edges.resolution_rule: the protocol wins: announcements carry no personal data and never request identifiers or bank details by reply; anything personal reaches an employee only through the platform authenticated self-service path

edges.why_related: clients want the outgoing provider cancelled immediately to stop paying it, while reconciliation depends on that provider records, cooperation and final filings
edges.resolution_rule: retrieval and reconciliation come first: keep the outgoing relationship alive until records are retrieved, the reconciliation is closed and the readiness gate is green, and treat the overlap fee as the price of not losing the evidence

edges.why_related: a wrong accumulator does not fail visibly; it produces wrong withholding for the rest of the year and surfaces later as a correction or an amendment
a deduction migrated with the wrong tax treatment shows up as a taxable-wage and net-pay variance in the comparison, which is how it is caught
a missing or still-pending agency or banking authorization is a leading cause of a first run that calculates but cannot deposit or file
termination of the outgoing provider is scheduled only after the gate is green, so a client is never left without a way to pay anyone
the announcement and the employee tasks it triggers must complete before the first live run, not alongside it
each explained variance points back at a specific migrated field or rule, and the roster and configuration are corrected from what the comparison reveals
every post-cutover incident names a check the gate did not contain, and the checklist grows by exactly those items
both are proof-by-reconciliation controls that test the configuration against an external answer that already exists, one for calculation rules and one for reported history

conflict_axes.name: clean_cutover_boundary_vs_client_urgency
conflict_axes.description: The boundary that minimises migration and split-filing work is often months away, while the client wants relief from a failing provider now.
poles: cut over as soon as the client wants
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: price the earlier date in added workstreams and written split-filing responsibility, let the client choose explicitly, and never fund the earlier date by shortening verification

conflict_axes.name: verification_depth_vs_announced_go_live_date
conflict_axes.description: Parallel run and reconciliation consume the days the announced date has already committed, and they are the first things a pressured project tries to shorten.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the date moves and the standard holds; any exception is a written client-owned override recorded at the readiness gate

conflict_axes.name: operator_convenience_vs_least_privilege
conflict_axes.description: Broad access and shared credentials make the work fast, while narrow time-boxed roles make it defensible and cleanly reversible.
poles: take only the access the task needs
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: least privilege always wins; where the narrow grant cannot do the task, the task moves to the client rather than the grant widening

conflict_axes.name: being_helpful_vs_staying_inside_the_professional_boundary
conflict_axes.description: The client wants a direct answer on classification, exemption or taxability, and giving one is both the most helpful-feeling and the most dangerous act available.
poles: answer the question the client asked
route it to a licensed adviser
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: route it, in writing, with the facts assembled and no recommendation, and configure only what the client determines

conflict_axes.name: platform_capability_vs_client_actual_policy
conflict_axes.description: Where the platform cannot express the client policy exactly, the temptation is to reshape the policy quietly to fit the software.
poles: preserve the client policy as written
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: surface the gap in writing as a client decision with its consequences; never let configuration silently redefine a pay or leave policy

conflict_axes.name: replicate_the_prior_system_vs_configure_from_source_evidence
conflict_axes.description: Copying the outgoing configuration is fast and reproduces its errors; building from agency notices and plan documents is slower and correct.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: source documents govern every compliance-critical attribute; the prior configuration is a cross-check and a source of questions, never an authority

conflict_axes.name: early_provider_cancellation_savings_vs_overlap_safety
conflict_axes.description: Running both providers costs duplicate fees, while cancelling early risks losing records, final filings and any fallback if the new system is not ready.
poles: keep the overlap until the gate is green
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: retrieve records and close the reconciliation first, terminate only after the gate is green, and treat the overlap fee as insurance rather than waste

conflict_axes.name: employee_self_entry_vs_operator_speed
conflict_axes.description: Employee self-entry keeps identifiers and bank details out of the operator hands but depends on people who may not act before the deadline.
poles: collect the data centrally to move fast
have employees enter their own data
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to self-entry with tracked completion and a documented fallback path for stragglers, rather than reverting the whole roster to central collection

conflict_axes.name: immediate_disclosure_vs_complete_investigation
conflict_axes.description: After an error the operator wants a full explanation before telling the client, but correction and reversal windows close while the investigation runs.
poles: report immediately with what is known
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclose immediately with the facts known, the class of repair and the window, then continue investigating; the window governs the clock, not the completeness of the explanation

edge_cases.description: A remote employee living in another jurisdiction is discovered after the company and roster are already configured
edge_cases.trigger: a home address in the roster does not match the work location assumed at triage
edge_cases.mitigation: reopen triage for that worker, treat the registration question as an adviser escalation for the client, add the jurisdiction workstream with its agency lead time, and re-derive the go-live date rather than paying the worker under a jurisdiction nobody verified

edge_cases.description: An agency account or agent authorization is still pending when the readiness gate is reached
edge_cases.trigger: an application submitted on time has not been confirmed by the agency before the scheduled first run
edge_cases.mitigation: hold the gate amber, ask the platform what its documented interim handling is for an unconfirmed account, get the client written acceptance of the interim arrangement and its consequence, and otherwise move the date

edge_cases.description: The outgoing provider releases records slowly or partially after notice is given
edge_cases.trigger: registers, filed returns or deposit records are requested and not delivered in full
edge_cases.mitigation: have the client make the request as the account owner, retrieve everything downloadable before access ends, delay the termination date rather than the retrieval, and quarantine any balance that cannot be tied

edge_cases.description: An email arrives during onboarding asking to change an employee or company bank account
edge_cases.trigger: a bank-detail change request appears in an inbound message during the migration window
edge_cases.mitigation: verify out of band on a known contact before any action, never action from the message thread, record the verification, and remind the client contact that this rule is permanent rather than a migration precaution

edge_cases.description: A client must leave a failing provider immediately, forcing a mid-period cutover
edge_cases.trigger: the incumbent provider has missed a filing or a payday and the client cannot wait for a clean boundary
edge_cases.mitigation: accept the boundary but write the split-period responsibility down explicitly with all parties, expand the balance migration and reconciliation scope, and escalate any pre-cutover filing failure to the client and its adviser rather than attempting to repair it

edge_cases.description: A support or garnishment order is served on the client during the migration window
edge_cases.trigger: a new withholding order arrives between the roster load and the first live run
edge_cases.mitigation: treat it as an in-scope migration item immediately, configure it in whichever system will run the next payroll, confirm no period is missed across the cutover, and route any question about its application to the client adviser or the issuing authority

edge_cases.description: The balances the client provides do not tie to the returns already filed for the year
edge_cases.trigger: the reconciliation worksheet shows a difference with no timing explanation
edge_cases.mitigation: quarantine the untied figures rather than loading or plugging them, classify the difference as migration error, prior-provider error or boundary timing, and refer any prior-period reporting issue in writing to the client and its adviser

edge_cases.description: The client wants to go live with unexplained parallel-run variances still open
edge_cases.trigger: the announced date arrives before the variance log is closed
edge_cases.mitigation: recommend moving the date, and if the client insists, record a written override naming each open variance, its possible consequence and the client acceptance, and prioritise those items in the first-run pre-approval review

edge_cases.description: Terminated employees with balances are missing from the prior-system export
edge_cases.trigger: the export contains only currently active workers
edge_cases.mitigation: reconcile worker counts against the year registers rather than against the current headcount, request the full-year population, and load terminated workers with their balances so annual statements can be produced from one system

edge_cases.description: The platform cannot express the client written time-off or accrual policy
edge_cases.trigger: a carryover, tiered accrual or waiting-period rule has no configuration equivalent
edge_cases.mitigation: document the gap and the options in writing, let the client decide whether to change the policy or to track the difference outside the system, and record whichever choice the client makes rather than configuring an approximation quietly

edge_cases.description: The owner asks the operator to decide whether a long-standing contractor should be on payroll
edge_cases.trigger: a determination question is put directly to the operator during setup
edge_cases.mitigation: state the boundary plainly, describe the pattern factually in writing without a recommendation, refer the question to the client adviser, and configure only what the client subsequently determines and records

edge_cases.description: The first pay date lands next to a bank holiday, shortening the funding window
edge_cases.trigger: the pay calendar places the first live run against a shortened banking window
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm the platform shifted deadline for that run in writing, tell the client the earlier funding requirement in plain terms, add slack by processing earlier, and avoid choosing such a date for a first run wherever the calendar allows

workflow.action: Frame the onboarding project and triage the client complexity
workflow.description: Write the deliverable list, walk the complexity driver checklist with evidence, build the dependency register with an owner and a date per item, and derive a go-live date from the drivers and the longest lead time rather than from client hope
workflow.artifact: onboarding plan with complexity classification and dated dependency register
workflow.gate: every driver has an evidenced answer, every register item has an owner and a due date, and the go-live date is derived and the stop rule stated in writing

workflow.action: Write the three-party service boundary map and the escalation classes
workflow.description: Assign every onboarding and recurring duty to the platform, the service layer or the client, state the operator negatives, and name the question classes that will always be routed to a licensed adviser
workflow.artifact: responsibility map with negatives and escalation class list
workflow.gate: no duty is unassigned or shared, and the client has been told at onboarding which questions will always be routed out

workflow.action: Stand up secure intake and obtain the authorization set
workflow.description: Open the auditable intake channel, prefer employee self-entry, then obtain platform roles, agency third-party authorizations and banking authorization at the narrowest scope that performs each task, recording holder, scope and revocation
workflow.artifact: authorization register and secure intake channel in use
workflow.gate: each required authorization class is granted or applied for with a tracked date, no operator grant exceeds its task, and the client retains owner-level control

workflow.action: Choose the cutover boundary and agree the responsibility split in writing
workflow.description: Compare year, quarter and mid-period cutover on migration burden and split filings, check agency lead times and the client business calendar, and get the outgoing provider and the client to confirm who covers each period
workflow.artifact: cutover decision record with written split-period responsibility
workflow.gate: every deposit, return and statement covering the cutover period is assigned to exactly one named party, confirmed by that party

workflow.action: Establish tax accounts, their attributes and agent linkage
workflow.description: Confirm the legal entity identity as agencies hold it, track each registration for every jurisdiction the workforce touches, read rate and deposit frequency from agency notices, link accounts into the platform and record where it acts as agent
workflow.artifact: jurisdiction account matrix with source documents and agent status
workflow.gate: every jurisdiction has evidenced identifiers, rate and frequency entered and platform-validated, and agent status is recorded per account with the performing party named where the platform is not agent

workflow.action: Configure the pay calendar, categories and accrual rules
workflow.description: Build the pay-period calendar with shifted pay dates and processing deadlines, configure every pay category in use, set the workweek as the client determined it, and check the written time-off policy against platform capability
workflow.artifact: configured pay rules and a client-confirmed pay calendar
workflow.gate: the calendar is confirmed by the client and every prior-system category and accrual rule has a counterpart or a written accepted difference

workflow.action: Migrate the employee roster with field-level validation
workflow.description: Map each field class from the prior register with its source of truth, keep home address and work location distinct, re-collect withholding elections where the source is unreliable, and include terminated workers who hold balances
workflow.artifact: loaded roster with validation exception log
workflow.gate: all validations pass or have a recorded disposition, and worker counts reconcile to the prior register including terminated workers

workflow.action: Rebuild deductions, contributions and active withholding orders
workflow.description: Recreate each item with its amount or formula, its tax treatment from the plan document, and its named remitter, and treat every active order as an evidenced legal instrument with a continuity check across the cutover
workflow.artifact: deduction and order schedule with treatment, remitter and evidence per item
workflow.gate: every prior-system item exists with treatment and remitter recorded or is confirmed dropped in writing by the client, and no active order has a gap period

workflow.action: Load year-to-date balances and tie them to filed returns
workflow.description: Load employee and employer accumulators from registers, filed returns and deposit records, re-extract them from the new system after loading, and reconcile per jurisdiction and tax class on a documented worksheet
workflow.artifact: balance load with source citations and the reconciliation worksheet
workflow.gate: every loaded figure ties to a source document, the re-extract matches source employee by employee, and every difference has a cause class and an owner with nothing plugged

workflow.action: Set up and test the money chain, then have the client announce the change
workflow.description: Capture and verify employee payment methods, authorise and test the company funding debit, confirm the funding deadline in writing, then have the client send the employee announcement with its task list and its no-data rule
workflow.artifact: verified payment methods, tested funding authorization and the sent employee announcement
workflow.gate: every payment method is verified or has a documented alternate path, the funding deadline is confirmed by the client, and the announcement was sent by the client carrying no personal data and no request for details by reply

workflow.action: Run the parallel verification and close every variance
workflow.description: Recompute an already-paid period in the new configuration without paying, compare line by line for every employee and category including unusual cases, and drive each variance to a named cause and disposition
workflow.artifact: variance log with cause and disposition per line
workflow.gate: zero unexplained variances remain, and every explained one is either a client-approved configuration change or a prior-system error the client has been told about

workflow.action: Pass the readiness gate, sequence the provider exit, supervise the first run and hand off
workflow.description: Walk the checklist to green with evidence, only then schedule the outgoing provider termination and the first live run, review the run before client approval and confirm debit, payments and tax accrual afterwards, then build the compliance calendar and close the evidence file with client sign-off
workflow.artifact: signed readiness gate, provider close-out statement, first-run supervision record, acknowledged compliance calendar and closed onboarding file
workflow.gate: every gate item is green on evidence or carries a written client override, the outgoing provider close-out is in writing, post-run confirmations are recorded, and the calendar and file are acknowledged and signed

priority_rationale: The frame, the three-party boundary map, the escalation classes and the confidentiality protocol come first because every later decision inherits from them: what the project owes, who owns each duty, which questions leave the operator entirely, and how sensitive data may be handled at all. Complexity triage and the cutover choice follow, because they set the scope and the date that the rest of the project must live inside. Authorizations and tax accounts precede migration because their agency lead times are the longest and least controllable dependency in the plan. Pay rules precede the roster, the roster precedes deductions and orders, and both precede year-to-date balances, because each layer is loaded against structures the previous one created. Verification then sits between migration and cutover by design: the parallel run proves the calculation rules and the filed-return reconciliation proves the history, and only when both are closed does the readiness gate authorise a provider exit and a first live run. Supervision, correction paths, the compliance calendar and the signed evidence file come last because they convert a configured system into a running relationship with an owner for every obligation and a record of every decision.

dominance_rules.rule: Confidentiality and least privilege dominate speed and convenience in every data and access decision
dominance_rules.rationale: the identifiers, wage histories and bank credentials moving during onboarding cannot be un-exposed, and the obligations attached to losing them fall on both the client and the operator
dominance_rules.trigger: any choice between a faster intake or access path and a narrower one
dominance_rules.action: take the narrower path; refuse identifiers on unapproved channels and refuse authority wider than the task, even when the client offers it

dominance_rules.rule: Primary source evidence dominates recollection and inherited configuration on every compliance-critical attribute
dominance_rules.rationale: agency notices, plan documents and filed returns are what agencies and carriers will hold the client to, while the prior system and human memory carry errors forward invisibly
dominance_rules.trigger: a rate, deposit frequency, tax treatment or balance is about to be set from what the prior provider had or what someone remembers
dominance_rules.action: configure from the source document, cite it in the file, and treat the prior configuration only as a cross-check that raises questions

dominance_rules.rule: The readiness gate dominates the announced go-live date
dominance_rules.rationale: a moved date costs one difficult conversation while a missed or wrong payday costs employee trust, potential penalties and usually the client
dominance_rules.trigger: the gate is not all green as the announced first pay date approaches
dominance_rules.action: move the date, or proceed only on a written client-owned override that names each open item, its risk and its mitigation

dominance_rules.rationale: classification, exemption, taxability and pay decisions carry employer liability and belong to the client and its licensed advisers
dominance_rules.trigger: a determination question is asked of the operator or a configuration would imply one
dominance_rules.action: route it in writing with the facts and no recommendation, and configure only what the client records as its determination

dominance_rules.rule: An active withholding order dominates migration convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: an order is a legal instrument served on the employer that does not pause for a system change, and a missed period harms both the employee and the client
dominance_rules.trigger: an order exists, is served or is amended at any point in the project
dominance_rules.action: configure it in whichever system runs the next payroll, verify withholding and remittance across the cutover with no gap, and route any interpretive question to the issuing authority or the client adviser

dominance_rules.rule: Money actually landing dominates process elegance on the first run
dominance_rules.rationale: employees judge the entire migration by whether they were paid on time, and an untested chain is the most common reason they are not
dominance_rules.trigger: the first live run approaches with any part of the payment or funding chain unverified
dominance_rules.action: move the date or pay the affected workers by a documented alternate method, and never rely on an unverified account for a first payday

dominance_rules.rule: Immediate disclosure of an error dominates finishing the investigation
dominance_rules.rationale: correction, reversal and off-cycle windows close on their own schedule, and a client who hears about an error from an employee stops trusting the operator entirely
dominance_rules.trigger: any indication that a run, deposit, filing or payment is wrong
dominance_rules.action: tell the client the same day with the facts known, the repair class and the window, then continue the investigation

dominance_rules.rule: Written responsibility assignment dominates assumption at every boundary
dominance_rules.rationale: the two catastrophic outcomes at a cutover, an obligation nobody filed and an obligation two parties filed, both come from an assumption nobody wrote down
dominance_rules.trigger: any period, filing, deposit or duty that spans the cutover or the platform boundary
dominance_rules.action: obtain written confirmation from the responsible party, and treat any duty without one as unowned and unresolved

dominance_rules.rule: Out-of-band verification dominates any instruction to change bank details
dominance_rules.rationale: payroll redirection fraud targets exactly this data at exactly this moment, and an inbound message is not evidence of who sent it
dominance_rules.trigger: any request to add or change employee or company banking details, from any channel
dominance_rules.action: verify on a known contact through a different channel before acting, and record the verification

dominance_rules.rule: Verified jurisdiction facts dominate assumptions carried from another client
dominance_rules.rationale: obligations differ by jurisdiction and change over time, so a rule that was right for one client or one year is not evidence for another
dominance_rules.trigger: an obligation, threshold or schedule is about to be applied from experience rather than from a current source
dominance_rules.action: verify the current rule for this client jurisdiction from the agency or platform source, or escalate it to the client adviser before acting

anti_rework_rules.rule: Triage the complexity drivers with evidence before quoting any go-live date
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a date built on an imagined client that collapses when a second jurisdiction, an order or a benefit arrangement appears mid-project

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the service boundary map before configuring anything
anti_rework_rules.prevents: duties discovered as ownerless after go-live, when reassigning them means renegotiating the relationship rather than filling in a cell

anti_rework_rules.rule: Start agency registrations and authorizations before the migration work begins
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a completed migration waiting weeks on an agency lead time that was never on anyone critical path

anti_rework_rules.rule: Configure pay categories, calendar and accrual rules before loading any worker
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a roster loaded against categories that do not exist yet, which has to be reworked worker by worker once they do

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record the client determinations before configuring the workers they govern
anti_rework_rules.prevents: workers set up on the operator assumption and then reclassified after payrolls have already run under the wrong treatment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Rebuild deductions, contributions and orders before loading year-to-date accumulators
anti_rework_rules.prevents: balances loaded against accumulators that do not exist, forcing the whole balance load to be redone

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tie balances to filed returns before starting the parallel run
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a variance investigation that chases calculation rules when the real fault is an untied opening balance

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the payment and funding chain before the client announces the date to employees
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an announced first payday that has to be retracted, which costs the client credibility with its own staff

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the outgoing provider engaged until records are retrieved and the gate is green
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a reconciliation that cannot be completed and a client with no fallback because access ended early

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the compliance calendar from this client accounts and configuration rather than from a template
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a first quarter after go-live spent discovering obligations that a generic calendar never listed

iteration_protocol.trigger: a dependency register item passes its due date
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive the go-live date from the remaining lead times, tell the client immediately, and move the date rather than compressing verification

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new complexity driver appears, such as a worker in another jurisdiction or a newly served order
iteration_protocol.action: reopen the triage, add the workstream and its agency lead time, and re-check the account matrix and the roster fields it touches

iteration_protocol.trigger: the parallel run produces a variance with no identified cause
iteration_protocol.action: trace it to the specific field or rule, correct it at the owning work unit, and re-run the comparison rather than accepting the variance as rounding

iteration_protocol.trigger: a reconciliation difference is classified as a prior-provider reporting error
iteration_protocol.action: quarantine the affected balance, refer the issue in writing to the client and its adviser with the worksheet, and do not adjust the new system to make totals agree

iteration_protocol.trigger: any configuration or data change is made after the readiness gate was marked green
iteration_protocol.action: reopen the affected gate items, re-verify them with evidence, and re-run the parallel comparison for anything touching calculation

iteration_protocol.trigger: the first live run produces an incident of any class
iteration_protocol.action: classify the repair and its window, disclose to the client the same day, execute the repair with its owner, and add the missed check to the pre-approval review and the gate checklist

iteration_protocol.trigger: a request arrives to add or change banking details for an employee or the company
iteration_protocol.action: verify out of band on a known contact before acting, record the verification, and re-brief the client contact on the permanence of the rule

iteration_protocol.trigger: an agency notice changes a rate, deposit frequency or filing obligation
iteration_protocol.action: verify the current requirement from the notice, update the platform configuration and the compliance calendar line, and record the change in the onboarding file
